content: To create a critical pathways page, follow these detailed steps: 1. Select a Topic: Begin by choosing a topic of interest from the Resident Survival Guide page. Assign a name to the selected topic. A visual example of what a critical pathways page looks like is provided for reference. You can click on the provided link to select a topic. 2. Use the Algorithm as a Reference: Access the algorithm for the selected topic in the Resident Survival Guide. To do this, click on the Resident Survival Guide icon located at the top right corner of the page. Use the first branch point of the algorithm as a guide to construct the first question. 3. Provide Answers to the First Question: Develop answers to the first question. There may be two or more possible answers. Ensure that the provided answers are linked to their corresponding pages on WikiDoc. A link is provided to guide you on how to create these links. 4. Define and Add Action Items: For the first question, provide clear definitions and action items. When necessary, include references to support the definitions. A link is provided to guide you on how to add references. 5. Proceed to the Next Branch Point: Use the second branch point of the algorithm, following each answer, as a reference to construct the second question. Repeat the steps of constructing questions, providing answers, linking pages, and adding definitions and action items. 6. Finalize the Critical Pathways Page: Once the critical pathways page is complete, add the critical pathways icon to the main page of the topic you worked on. For example, if you created a critical pathways page for hyperkalemia, include a link to it on the hyperkalemia page using the critical pathways icon. 7. Definitions: Ensure that the definitions of the answers are provided and referenced when possible. For example, metabolic acidosis can be defined as a condition characterized by an increased production of hydrogen ions (H+) or the inability of the kidneys to generate bicarbonate (HCO3-). The anion gap, calculated as [Na+] ([Cl-] + [HCO3-]), is a useful diagnostic tool. The normal reference range for the anion gap is between 8 and 16 mEq/L. 8. Action Items: Determine the next steps in patient management based on the constructed pathway. For instance, in the case of metabolic acidosis, consider whether to check for respiratory compensation or whether to administer bicarbonate therapy. These decisions should be guided by the clinical context and supported by evidence-based references.
